messages.terco.source-exact.62: A modern popular Brazilian devotion for the struggles people actually face - illness, temptation, fear, the long fight for a family or a livelihood. It is prayed on a standard rosary, in plain Portuguese words that ask God for strength and courage, and it ends with the Salve Rainha, the Hail Holy Queen.
messages.terco.source-exact.63: A rosary resting in open hands
messages.terco.source-exact.64: The Terço da Batalha is prayed on an ordinary rosary - large beads, small beads, and the cross.

messages.terco.source-exact.71: . It is not the official Dominican Rosary, and it is not an official liturgical text of the Church. Popular devotions like this one are the people's way of praying their struggles - legitimate and loved, but they carry no promise of guaranteed results. God remains free; we remain askers.
messages.terco.source-exact.72: The Portuguese text below is the source of truth for this page. Every translation is labeled as a translation, and the wording follows the version shared in the source - older variants of this devotion use different lines, and we do not mix them in.
messages.terco.source-exact.74: You need only an ordinary rosary and the intention you are carrying.
messages.terco.source-exact.75: Hold the struggle in mind. Invite your guardian angel to pray with you.

messages.terco.source-exact.77: Pelo sinal da Santa Cruz, livrai-nos, Deus nosso Senhor, dos nossos inimigos. Em nome do Pai, do Filho e do Espírito Santo. Amém.
messages.terco.source-exact.78: Then pray the Creed, one Our Father, and three Hail Marys (standard texts).
